newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea's 3-yr yields hit new 18-month high.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's 3-yr yields hit new 18-month high.

text.p: South Korea's benchmark three-year corporate bond yields hit a new 18-month intraday high of 12.89 percent on Friday due to worries over the Sammi Group financial difficulties, brokers said.
The level was the highest since September 19, 1995, when the yields closed at 12.90 percent.
Brokers said sentiment deteriorated after Sammi Steel sought protection from creditors on Tuesday along with other affiliates.
"Liquidity, especially in the short-term money market, showed signs of drying up," said Lee Chang-woo of Samsung Securities.
The three-year yields closed Thursday at 12.85 percent, while the three-month CDs ended at 13.65 percent.
